references.text: When Jesus himself stood among the disciples, they were terrified and afraid (Luke 24:37). The same reaction of fear (ἔμφοβοι) that the women showed at the tomb.
Cornelius was terrified when he saw the angel (Acts 10:4). The same Greek word (ἔμφοβος) is used for the fear response in a heavenly encounter.

Daniel fell with his face to the ground when he received a vision (Daniel 10:9). Bowing one's face to the ground is a typical reaction to divine revelation, just as the women bowed their faces to the ground.
The travelers on the road to Emmaus reported that the women had seen angels who said Jesus was alive (Luke 24:23). The angels' message confirms that Jesus is "the living one", not among the dead.
Jesus says: "I am the living one. I was dead, and see, I live forever" (Revelation 1:18). Christ is described as "the living one" (τὸν ζῶντα), the same expression the angels used at the tomb.

Jesus showed himself alive to the apostles after his suffering (Acts 1:3). The angels' question, "Why do you seek the living among the dead?", points forward to his many appearances as the living one.
Paul proclaims that Christ, raised from the dead, no longer dies (Romans 6:9). Jesus no longer belongs among the dead but is the living one—exactly what the angels conveyed to the women.

When the women entered the tomb, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus (Luke 24:3). The empty tomb is the background for the angels' question: it makes no sense to look for the living among the dead.
In Mark's parallel account, the young man in white says: "He has risen; he is not here" (Mark 16:6). The same message is conveyed: Jesus is not among the dead.

In Matthew's parallel account, the angel says: "Do not be afraid! I know you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified. He is not here; he has risen" (Matthew 28:5-6). The same event with similar angelic testimony about the resurrection.
